public_body: Gloucester Community Arts Charter School Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found three violations: executive session strayed beyond its purpose (Jan 6, 2010), the Marsh contract was negotiated in executive session, and the Sept 13, 2010 emergency meeting was improperly noticed. Other allegations were not violations. Ordered compliance, annual training for 2011-2012, notice submissions, and an executive session minutes review.

allegations.summary: Complaint 1: the Board went beyond the January 6, 2010 executive session's stated purpose by discussing the revised enrollment policy.
allegations.key_passage: Based upon our review of the open and executive session minutes we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law with regard to this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint 1: the Board improperly discussed whether to continue as a charter school, beyond the purposes allowed for the January 6, 2010 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this portion of the discussion was inappropriately held during executive session and was therefore a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint 2: the Board deliberated on the contract with Head of School candidate Ljuba Marsh in executive session, which was not a permitted purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the deliberation undertaken by the Board in executive session with regard to the contract with Ms. Marsh was in violation of the Open Meeting Law in effect on December 16, 2010.

allegations.summary: Complaint 2: the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting on the appointment of Matthew Gallup as Interim Director, with no open-session discussion.
allegations.key_passage: it does raise concerns about the manner in which deliberations occur and are memorialized by the Board.

allegations.summary: Complaint 2: the Board deliberated outside a properly posted open session or executive session about changing the school's facility location.
allegations.key_passage: there is not enough evidence to find with certainty that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint 2: the Board changed the enrollment plan and accepted applications for grades 4-7 without a deliberation or decision in a public meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We are satisfied that these responses address the concerns raised by the complainant.

allegations.summary: Complaint 3: the Board held an emergency meeting on September 13, 2010 about the school's delayed opening and location, though leadership knew of the need more than 48 hours earlier.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by inappropriately convening an emergency meeting in contravention of the posting requirements of the law on September 13, 2010.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18- 25.
Attend a training on the Open Meeting Law annually during each of the next two calendar years (2011 and 2012), and certify to this office that every member of the Board has attended that training.

Submit a copy to the Division of Open Government of any and all meeting notices required by the Open Meeting Law and posted by the full Board or its subcommittees for the next two calendar years (2011 and 2012) commencing immediately following the issuance of this determination, and concluding on December 31, 2012.

Review all unreleased executive session minutes to determine whether the purpose for having entered executive session in each circumstance still exists, and release executive session minutes where doing so would no longer frustrate the purpose for having entered into the executive session.
